name: ascii-matrix
summary: Glyph rain in a character panel: 80 columns, each with a block head and a trail that grows and shrinks by a row a frame, with the copy on a card over the corner.

cols.description: Characters across the panel. style.css scales the type so exactly this many fit its width, so this is the rain's resolution rather than its size.

rows.description: Character rows. Sets the panel's height, since the type is scaled to the width.

resetChance.description: A column restarts at the top when Math.random() clears this. Upstream's 0.985 in matrix.js; lower it and the rain restarts more often.

deviations.what: The first character of the glyph alphabet is U+0020 SPACE. Upstream writes U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE there.
deviations.why: U+3000 is not in any face on a Latin monospace stack, so the browser substitutes a CJK font and renders it at double advance width. Every row that draws one shears out of alignment from that column on, which stops the grid being a grid. It is invisible upstream because the glyph is blank and only the columns give it away, and it is broken at the pinned commit rather than by anything the port does.

deviations.what: The effect object with start(pre, colsRows) / stop() becomes mount(el, opts) over ../_shared/ascii-grid.js. Upstream's start() body is make(w, h, settings), upstream's step() is the closure make returns, and `pre.textContent = out; requestAnimationFrame(step)` is `return out`.
deviations.why: The effect contract is mount/update/destroy. The rewrite is mechanical and the drop, trail and wrap logic between those two lines is untouched.

deviations.what: Upstream keeps its rAF id as this.loopId on the single exported effect object. Here it is a closure per mount inside ascii-grid.js.
deviations.why: Two mounts of one effect would share that id, so the second stop() orphans the first loop. Several panels on one page have to be independent, which is a case a single full-screen demo never has.

deviations.what: The grid is declared as cols and rows (--fx-cols / --fx-rows, 80 x 34) and style.css scales the type with a container query so exactly that many characters fit the panel. main.js's colsRows(), which measures the viewport against an 8x12 character guess and caps at makeDims(120, 60), is dropped.
deviations.why: A section does not own the viewport, and a measured grid cannot match an authored resting frame -- the frame is written at fixed dimensions, so a live grid of other dimensions reflows the instant the script takes over. Declaring it also keeps the rain's proportions from 375 up.

deviations.what: snippet.html carries an authored resting frame: a real frame of this effect at the same 80 x 34 grid, dumped from index.js. destroy() restores it.
deviations.why: Upstream ships no static fallback at all -- its <pre> is empty until the script runs. The effect contract requires the section to look finished on CSS alone, and a destroy mid-run would otherwise freeze on whichever frame was in flight.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion mount() returns without starting the loop, leaving the authored frame in place.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. The frame is already the finished picture.

deviations.what: util.js's visibilityPause is dropped; an IntersectionObserver in ascii-grid.js idles the loop while the section is off screen instead.
deviations.why: Upstream re-activates on tab focus because it re-measures the viewport, which a declared grid never needs, and rAF already stops in a hidden tab. The off-screen case is the one a full-screen demo cannot have and a page with three panels does.
